models_evaluated: eight prominent LLMs (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Safety interventions offered across simulated multi-turn delusion scenarios
links.effect: Models offered safety interventions in roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS 0.37 ± 0.48); 51/128 (39.8%) of scenarios had no safety interventions offered.
links.quote: Models frequently enabled harmful user requests (mean HES of 0.69 $\pm$0.84) and offered safety interventions in only roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS of 0.37 $\pm$0.48).

links.outcome: Delusion confirmation and safety intervention across evolving multi-turn simulated conversations, explicit versus implicit
links.effect: Mean DCS 0.91 ± 0.88; implicit scenarios had more delusion confirmation, more harm enablement, and fewer interventions (p < .001).
links.quote: Performance was significantly worse in implicit scenarios, models were more likely to confirm delusions and enable harm while offering fewer interventions (p < .001).

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking LLM psychogenicity (delusion confirmation and harm enablement) in multi-turn conversations with vulnerable users

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM safety risks regarding delusion reinforcement and harm enablement using simulated multi-turn conversational scenarios (Psychosis-bench), but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
